title: Slow-Cooker Chicken Curry
subtitle: Anglo-Indian chicken curry cooked low and slow
excerpt: Chicken thighs simmered in a well-spiced tomato-and-onion gravy for 6 hours in the slow cooker until the meat is tender and the sauce is rich. An easy weeknight curry that starts itself in the morning.

recipe.sourceNotes: The slow cooker version of a British-style chicken curry follows the same principles as a conventional stovetop curry but shifts the active cooking to a brief morning prep: brown the chicken and fry the spices, then leave the slow cooker to do the work. Chicken thighs are used in preference to breast because they remain moist over the long cooking period and do not dry out. Naan or rice are the natural accompaniments.

content.text: The spices must be cooked in oil before the liquid goes in: this step, called blooming, removes the raw edge from the spices and deeply improves the finished flavour. Cook the onion base and spices until the oil separates from the paste before adding the tomatoes. The slow cooker holds moisture, so less liquid is needed than in a stovetop version.
Heat the vegetable oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat. Brown the chicken thighs for 3 minutes per side. Transfer to the slow cooker.

In the same pan, cook the onion over medium heat for 8 minutes until golden. Add the garlic and ginger and cook for 1 minute. Add the cumin, coriander, turmeric, garam masala, and chilli powder. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring. Add the tomato puree and cook for 1 minute. Pour in the tinned tomatoes and stock.
Pour the sauce over the chicken in the slow cooker. Season with salt. Cook on LOW for 5 to 6 hours or HIGH for 3 to 4 hours.
Taste and adjust the seasoning. Scatter with fresh coriander and serve with rice or naan.
